note: These are the ones that bite the first stranger who signs up.

items.title: Email sign-in is capped at 2 messages an hour
items.detail: Supabase's built-in mailer is development only, and the app now offers email as a way in. The third person to request a link in an hour gets nothing. Needs Resend or Postmark wired in: a config change, no code.

items.title: Errors are shown but never recorded
items.detail: A crash raises the fatal banner and names the function, so the user sees it. Nothing is sent anywhere, so we never learn it happened. Needs a table plus a hook on the existing error listeners; no new vendor.

items.title: Legal pages predate half the app
items.detail: privacy.html and support.html were written before clips, live sessions, push notifications and photos existed, and use a different design language from the app. Apple requires the privacy policy to match what is actually collected.

items.title: Onboarding has never been walked as a genuinely new account
items.detail: Name, goal, detail, pace, plan, then pairing. Every path exists but has only ever been used by accounts that already had data. Empty states for a truly fresh account need the same pass the rest of the app got.

note: A direction has been reviewed and picked. Nothing here is live, and none of it blocks anyone until it is built for real.

items.title: The tiles-plus-sheet goal picker is a prototype, not the real onboarding step
items.detail: Mo compared the bubble cluster against two other directions after opening every bubble at once and finding 52 items cannot share one screen at any spacing, then picked tiles-plus-sheet: nine categories always visible as a grid, tap one for its full checklist in a bottom sheet, multi-select persists across categories. It runs for real in the sandbox walkthrough (renderGoalTilesPrototype / initGoalTiles in index.html), on the real nine-category research content, not placeholder. It has never been wired into the real onboarding step. The gallery's static Choosing a goal page still shows the earlier bubble concept and has not been rebuilt to match this direction.
items.where: index.html, renderGoalTilesPrototype / initGoalTiles; scripts/make-states.mjs Choosing a goal page is stale, still shows bubbles

items.title: Limits and injuries: the screen is prototyped, not built for real
items.detail: A health condition, an injury or an age is not a goal, it is a limit on how the goal gets trained for, so it was pulled out of the goal bubbles on 2026-09-09. The screen now exists as a prototype (renderLimitsPrototype in index.html, in the sandbox walkthrough after the body focus step): "Anything we should know?", eight body areas, six pieces of equipment you might not have, one optional free-text line, and a Skip for now that is a real button rather than small print. Shown AFTER the plan exists, never before, so it only ever makes an existing plan safer and never blocks somebody from getting one. The chip content itself is PLACEHOLDER and blocked on the engine, see the entry below. Still to do for real: somewhere to store it (the parallel of profiles.focus_groups), the engine reading it to drop or substitute movements, and the same answers being editable later from Setup. Deliberately only the STATED half; the measured half (an exercise quietly swapped away from every week) is the better signal and is being built engine-side separately under exercise_swaps / engine/preferences.mjs.

items.title: The body focus picker is in Setup, never in onboarding
items.detail: Built for real on 2026-09-09: Setup now has a Focus areas row that opens the picker as a settings page, and Save writes profiles.focus_groups and focus_chosen_at, which mo-knowledge/engine/focus.mjs reads to give each picked group 1.4x its weekly sets. Body impact's muscle viewer got the same save path behind a Focus on this button. Uses the actual purchased figure (knowledge/anatomy/rive-body.mjs, human_anatomy_advanced_v3.0.riv), the same asset Body Impact and the workout builder already render. A tap marks or unmarks the whole 14-group it belongs to (RIVE_TO_APP_GROUP / APP_GROUP_TO_RIVE_MUSCLES, painted in the app accent green on both artboards, front delts and rear delts both from either one). Went through a tap-to-zoom pass and then a pinch-to-zoom pass; neither turned out to be wanted, so there is no zoom at all, tapping never moves the camera. Four is the cap, so Full body is gone and only Clear all is left. What is still not built: onboarding never asks. Somebody who never opens Setup never picks a focus, so the engine sees null for every new account, and the goal's own priority is all it has to go on.

items.title: The limits screen's content has to come from the engine, not from the screen
items.detail: The eight body areas and six pieces of equipment on the limits screen were written to have something real to tap in the prototype. Neither list is derived from anything, and checking them against the exercise library says they are wrong in two different ways. An answer is only worth collecting if something downstream can act on it; offering a limit nothing can honour is a promise the plan quietly breaks. EQUIPMENT: the library records exactly five values it can filter on (bodyweight, dumbbell, barbell, cable, machine), and 60 of its exercises record no equipment at all. Of the six the screen offers, three (Pull-up bar, Squat rack, Bench) do not exist in the engine in any form, so somebody can say they have no squat rack and nothing can honour it; meanwhile machine, which the engine CAN honour, is not offered. INJURIES: worse. There is no joint or pain concept in the library at all, an exercise records name, primary, secondary, equipment, level and that is the lot. The only way to act on 'my shoulder hurts' today is by proxy, dropping anything listing shoulders in primary or secondary, which is wrong in both directions at once: it drops most chest pressing (shoulders is a secondary on nearly all of it) while keeping plenty that genuinely loads a bad shoulder. So the engine owns this content. Equipment should be whatever the library can actually filter on, with the 60 unmarked exercises resolved first. Injuries need a concept that does not exist yet, most likely a per-exercise contraindication or joint-load tag, before a body area is worth putting on the screen at all.
items.where: index.html PROTO_LIMIT_HURTS / PROTO_LIMIT_MISSING; knowledge/exercise-library/*.mjs equipment and (missing) joint fields

note: Nothing here can move without an account, a click, or a decision only you can make.

items.title: Sign in with Apple needs the Developer account
items.detail: Apple requires it once any social login is offered, so it blocks App Store submission. The keys cannot be generated without the paid account. The sign-in screen already has room for the button.

items.title: Jawa is still not a collaborator on the repo
items.detail: Her CODEOWNERS entries point at @jawaabdulal now, but a CODEOWNERS line does nothing until she has repo access. The deploy token cannot add her: it is fine-grained with no Administration permission.

items.title: meridian-web-studio has push access and I do not know who that is
items.detail: A second collaborator with write access to the repo, account created 2026-08-01, no activity on it. Worth confirming who it is or removing it before real users exist.

items.title: Photo retention was never decided
items.detail: Raised in the strategy meeting and left open. Proof photos expire after 30 days. Progress photos tied to a goal have no policy at all, and storage cost was explicitly called a real constraint.

note: Real features that a PWA genuinely cannot do. They all arrive with the same Capacitor step.

items.title: The timer stops when the app is backgrounded
items.detail: Deliberate today, so time asleep is not counted, but the ask was for it to keep running like a navigation app. Needs genuine background execution, which the web cannot give.

items.title: Hands-free voice logging
items.detail: Costed 2026-09-06. Safari has never shipped the speech recognition API, so this cannot be built as a PWA at all. Native gives Apple's on-device Speech framework, but foreground only: push to talk, never always listening. Camera hand gestures are the one option that works in the web app today.
items.where: Capacitor, or MediaPipe in the web app

note: Known, chosen on purpose, and written down so the reasoning is not lost.

items.title: Every write still refetches every table
items.detail: loadAll() runs after almost every write. It is one parallel batch now, and it no longer repaints Home when Home is not on screen, but it still refetches everything rather than updating what changed. Fine at current volume.

items.title: Two tables are fetched in full, unbounded
items.detail: fit_entries and exercise_logs are read whole. Deliberately not windowed: personal records need a true all-time max per exercise and the calendar needs the true first entry ever, so a rolling window would make both silently wrong. Indexed on (email, entry_date) in the meantime.

items.title: The cron secret is inlined in the database
items.detail: Vault is unavailable on this project, so the shared secret sits in the cron job commands and inside the live-start trigger function body. Anyone with database access can read it. Accepted for now; it is not a user credential.

items.title: The gallery does not cover four tabs
items.detail: Workout, Body, Progress and Setup are not in here. They are covered instead by the app harness, which runs the real app against fixture data and screenshots every tab.

items.title: Two new sheets are unverified visually
items.detail: The encouragement composer and the askForName sheet that replaced the browser prompts passed the boot check and reuse the app's existing composer pattern, but have not been screenshotted. The browser harness kept getting killed the day they shipped.

items.title: Two of the 11 milestone badges lean on a proxy, not a real record
items.detail: Bodyweight Bench compares a bench press log against the most recent scale weigh-in, not the body weight at the moment of that specific set, since the app has never recorded one alongside the other. 1 Year reads the accepted partnership's responded_at, which is real, but nothing else about a pairing's history is tracked, so if that ever needs correcting there is no second source to check it against. Both are honest best-efforts, verified against realistic fixture data (run node scripts/badge-check-test.mjs), not guesses. Fifteen more badge ideas (rest-day-safe consistency ones, a comeback PR, cheering counts, evenly-matched weeks) are still only written down, with no icon and no check function.

note: Kept so they do not come back around as fresh ideas.

items.title: No music integration
items.detail: Showing what your partner is listening to via Spotify was overruled in the strategy meeting: music apps already play in the background, people use different services, and it is not core. Do not build it.

items.title: Live streaming is not the cheering feature
items.detail: Deliberately not FaceTime or a live stream, which was agreed to be too expensive. A short clip that loops on their session screen and then disappears was the chosen shape, and it shipped.
